Anya: Heads-up — Prod customer (AcmeHealth) opened an escalation: reranking endpoint returning all-zero scores and some 400s when they try to pass candidates via cURL from their CI.
Jared: Oof. Which endpoint exactly? /v1/rerank?
Anya: Yep. They say it worked earlier this week but now they get: "scores: [0,0,0,...]" for every request. Also sometimes they hit "400: candidates exceed max length".
Maya: Do we have the original request payload from them?
Anya: They attached a minimal repro. Copying the main bits below (they ran this in GitLab CI on Windows runner):

Anya: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '@payload.json'
```

Anya: payload.json they used:
```json
{
  "query": "What is the best chair for back pain?",
  "candidates": "[\"kneeling chair\", \"ergonomic desk chair\"]",
  "top_k": 5
}
```

Anya: Notice candidates is a string containing JSON array (because their helper script does a stringify step). They said docs show an example with a literal array and another with @file which confused them.
Jared: Ah, passing the array as a string would explain the all-zero scores — model interprets the candidate as one long token? Also max length validation could see the string length and trigger candidate-length errors.
Kevin: Also Windows GitLab runner + single quotes in the examples can be misleading. On PowerShell you need double quotes or escape; some folks end up embedding the JSON as a string into the value of candidates.
Maya: Do we log input parsing errors downstream? Can we detect when candidates is a string vs array and give a clearer error instead of scoring zeros?
Anya: Customer logs show our service accepted the request and returned 200 with scores [0...]. No parse error on our side, because our schema allows candidates: array<string> OR string? Looks like our backend casted it to a single candidate (the literal string) and scored accordingly.
Jared: That's a bug in the validation layer — we should reject non-array types for candidates with 400 and helpful msg. For now we can suggest a workaround to the customer and patch docs.
Anya: Customer also reported that our docs' curl example uses -d '{...}' and a separate example uses -d @file.json. The docs don't call out PowerShell quoting and @file behavior on Windows. They said their UI helper wrote the file with UTF-16 BOM which also confused our parser once (rare).
Maya: Actionable steps: 1) Provide immediate repro and fix steps to customer. 2) Add explicit PowerShell and Windows examples in docs. 3) Harden validation to return 400 with descriptive message. 4) Add a quick warning in rerank API doc about candidate count/size limits.
Kevin: For the immediate customer reply suggest they ensure candidates is an actual JSON array. Example curl for PowerShell (works on Windows):

Kevin: ```powershell
$body = @{
  query = 'What is the best chair for back pain?'
  candidates = @('kneeling chair','ergonomic desk chair')
  top_k = 5
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3

Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank' -Method Post -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:REDWOOD_KEY" } -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json'
```

Jared: Also share a simple POSIX curl example that avoids single-quote issues and shows inline JSON safely:

Jared: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"What is the best chair for back pain?","candidates":["kneeling chair","ergonomic desk chair"],"top_k":5}'
```

Anya: I replied to the customer with the PowerShell example + asked for the raw payload file to inspect BOM. Also asked if they could run a quick test using the inline curl to see if scores change.
SupportBot: permalink: https://app.redwood.ai/support/12345 — customer confirmed they tried the inline curl and now get non-zero scores.
Anya: Customer says inline worked. They attached the payload.json from CI; it indeed had candidates as a string and saved with UTF-16 LE BOM. That explains the earlier 400 and then silent scoring.
Maya: OK, plan for engineering: patch server-side validation to reject candidates when not an array (assign to Jared), add best-practice doc addendum for Windows/PowerShell examples (assign to Maya), and add a small ingest-time log when payload parsing sees unusual encodings (assign to Kevin). Also add a note about candidate count limits in the rerank doc.
Jared: I'll open a PR for validation + unit tests today. I'll include a check for BOM and explicit message like: "candidates must be a JSON array of strings; looks like you passed a string or encoded file — try using an array or ConvertTo-Json in PowerShell".
Maya: I'll update the docs and examples and include both curl and PowerShell copy-paste blocks, and a short troubleshooting FAQ entry.
Kevin: I'll add a small middleware to fail fast on UTF-16 BOM or coerce to UTF-8 and log if coercion happened.
Anya: Customer happy for now, will wait for the validation change. They asked that we also surface an example in Console (UI) when uploading candidates as a file so we show accepted formats.
Maya: Good idea — I'll add a UI hint for 'Upload as JSON array of strings' and a short sample.
Anya: Thanks team. I'll keep the ticket open until PRs are merged and docs updated. Closing interim loop with customer.
SupportBot: Ticket 12345 updated: status -> investigating, assigned -> Jared, Maya, Kevin. ETA docs patch: 48h.
Anya: :white_check_mark:
